text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "SchNet's filters see only the interatomic distances to neighbors. They are generated by a network that maps the roto-translationally invariant distances to filter values, and only radial filters are used [W2988055229#033][W3093149769#042]. The features therefore stay scalar and rotation-invariant [W4225405705#003]. NequIP's filters use the relative position vector, factored into a learnable radial function of the distance times spherical harmonics of the unit vector: F(r_ij) = R(r_ij)Y(l)_m(r̂_ij) [W4225405705#006]. This lets angular information enter the filters, and atom features become equivariant geometric tensors (scalars, vectors, higher-order tensors) rather than just invariant scalars [W4225405705#003][W4225405705#006]. Keeping only the 0 ⊗ 0 → 0 interaction reduces NequIP to a conventional invariant, SchNet-like convolution over scalar features [W4225405705#008]."}
